checks.finding: REQ-001 through REQ-006 each resolve to concrete, measurable acceptance criteria: exit codes and propagation narrative (AC-001), documented limitation phrasing (AC-002), timeout parsing with exit-2 rejection (AC-003), wall-clock margin plus liveness check (AC-004), exit code plus verdict-file absence (AC-005/AC-006), table completeness with non-empty disposition cells (AC-007/AC-008), literal-identifier plus trust/mitigation statement (AC-009/AC-010/AC-013), and passing regression suites reading the shared default (AC-011/AC-012). All requirements are observable or measurable enough to validate later.

Every stated goal in the Overview has a matching AC: failure-taxonomy completeness -> AC-001/AC-002; bounded invocation and fail-closed disposition -> AC-003/AC-004/AC-005/AC-006; OWASP + MCP checklist cross-reference -> AC-007/AC-008/AC-013; the five absent runtime trust surfaces -> AC-009/AC-010; and recording the panelist-timeout hole in the threat model -> AC-014 (new this round, resolving investigation OQ-3).

AC-004's per-runtime table states PowerShell escalation is Kill($true), 'the PowerShell analogue of the SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL escalation, not a second mechanism' (i.e. no soft step exists), then immediately frames the Edge-Case-7 PowerShell counterpart as 'a stub that does not exit on a close request' -- language presupposing a close request IS sent. TEST-004(b)'s PowerShell text repeats this and justifies it with wording identical to sub-case (a)'s justification ('distinguishes a real tree-kill from a parent that merely stopped waiting'), confirming no PowerShell-specific escalation behavior is actually being verified distinct from (a). A task author cannot tell whether the PowerShell runner must add a soft-close attempt before Kill($true) (contradicting 'not a second mechanism') or whether sub-case (b) is simply redundant with (a) for this runtime -- an ambiguity internal to the acceptance criteria/test text in a security-relevant kill mechanism, which is spec review's responsibility to resolve before implementation, not implementation review's to reinterpret. Sub-cases (a) and (c) of the same table remain adequately observable.

Non-goals section is explicit and specific: retries excluded with reasoning, the already-correct absent/error path is not to be restated, malformed-output handling is documented-not-implemented with file:line citation, the Codex agent-role surface is not to be re-documented, check-cross-model's logic is untouched, and vendor CLI pinning/vendoring is out of scope.

Baseline Constraints BL-001 through BL-005 state behavior-preservation for the absent/error path, an unmodified check-cross-model, extend-not-replace policy text with line citations, dual-runtime parity, and confirmation (via direct read of guard-invariants.generated.js:5) that no PROTECTED_GATE_SUFFIXES file is touched -- each material constraint implied by the requirements is stated explicitly.

The two high-risk claims in this specification -- a hung panelist stalling a critical security gate, and an unresolved residual risk in the threat model -- each have a planned validation surface: AC-004/AC-005/AC-006 with TEST-004/TEST-005/TEST-006 for the former, and AC-014 with TEST-014 for the latter.
